paper.title: Long-term effects of school size on students' outcomes
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement is printed and no Statistics Denmark project number is given. …

registers.name_in_paper: a data set containing actual school enrollment numbers each year obtained from The Danish IT Centre for Education and Research (UNI-C)
registers.role: treatment: school size, by year-school-grade level, aggregated to the school level

registers.name_in_paper: centrally registered grade 9 exit exam grades
registers.role: outcome: average grades in oral Math, written Math, oral Danish and written Danish

registers.name_in_paper: school district (catchment area) data, including the number of children in a specific age group and the fraction of immigrants
registers.role: instrument (catchment area size) and catchment area controls
variables_mentioned: number of children in the catchment area aged 7-16 years
share of non-Western immigrants and descendants in catchment area
log average earnings in catchment area

linkages: All children are linked to their parents through unique personal identifiers.
Street addresses are linked to school catchment areas; the link was only possible back to 1993, so for the grade 9 cohorts 1986-1992 the 1993 street address-catchment area link is used.
Students are linked to the school they attend in grade 9, and schools to UNI-C enrollment numbers.
Siblings are linked within families for the sibling fixed effect sample (only individuals with a sibling attending the same school).

sample.universe: The entire population of Danish children who attended grade 9 in public schools in the years 1986-2004
sample.unit_of_observation: individual student observed in grade 9 (one observation per student; if a child attends grade 9 more than once the first occurrence is used)
selection_rules: Non-missing personal identifiers and birth records: 1,158,401 (99.8%)
Did not live in the municipality of Viborg: 840,669 (72.4%)
Attended schools that did not receive students from feeder schools: 605,125 (52.1%)

construction_notes: School size in a given year is defined as the number of students in grades 0-9 in the school; in the regressions it enters as school size/100 ('school size is measured in hundredths of students').
Catchment area size in a given year is defined as the number of children in the catchment area aged 7-16 years at the end of the year.

The instrumental variable for school openings (closings) is the change in school size from one year to the next if a school opens (closes) in the municipality of the school; zero if no school opens (closes).
Outcomes (1)-(3) are measured 6 years after grade 9, i.e. at about age 22.
Inactivity: individuals are labelled inactive if they have neither completed nor are enrolled in an upper secondary education and their earnings are below DKK 40,000 (measured in year 2000 DKK).
Earnings at age 30 are annual deflated earnings, observed only for the cohorts attending grade 9 from 1986 to about 1998.
Grade 9 exit exam grade is the average of the grades in oral Math, written Math, oral Danish and written Danish; available only for grade 9 2002-2004.
All parental background variables are defined at the time the child is 15 years old, i.e. one year before a typical child completes grade 9.

Feeder-school exclusion: for each year the country proportion between cohort sizes in grade 9 and grade 5 is computed; a school whose school-specific proportion exceeds the country proportion by more than 10% is excluded.
For the grade 9 cohorts 1986-1992 the 1993 street address-catchment area link is used; the main results are reported to be robust to excluding these cohorts.
All standard errors are corrected for clustering at the school level.

claims.statement: Among grade 9 students in Danish public schools 1986-2004, a 100-student larger school is associated with a 0.8 percentage point higher probability of completing high school or vocational education, estimated by OLS with controls only.

register_source.value: The Danish IT Centre for Education and Research (UNI-C) school enrollment data, by year-school-grade level, aggregated to the school year; no Statistics Denmark register code or variable name is given

definition.value: Number of students in grades 0-9 in the school in the given year, divided by 100 ('school size is measured in hundredths of students'). The paper's definition of the effect is the total policy effect of school size, i.e. including both the direct effect and indirect effects such as an effect through class size.

timing.value: School size of the school in the year the student attends grade 9

outcome.label: Completion of high school or vocational education

definition.value: Binary indicator for whether the student has completed high school or vocational education and training 6 years after grade 9, i.e. at about age 22.

timing.value: 6 years after attending grade 9 (about age 22)

units.value: change in the probability of completing high school or vocational education (0-1 scale) per 100 additional students in the school

magnitude.interpretation: increasing school size by 100 students increases the probability of completing high school by 0.8 percentage points
